Teens Steal Kia Using Viral Hack, Ring Video Shows Them Jumping From Moving Car
10 photos
Photo: Screenshot from YouTube video
Two teenagers got inside a Kia, “hacked” it using a method that went viral on TikTok, and drove away before jumping out of the moving vehicle. This is what happened recently in Toledo, Ohio, where teens who are part of the infamous Kia Boys group can still find unpatched Kias and Hyundais quite easily.
The Kia Challenge started in 2022 when someone posted a video on TikTok to highlight a vulnerability in certain Kia and Hyundai models. The lack of an immobilizer in vehicles produced between 2011 and 2021 allows anyone to start the engines of these cars in a matter of seconds, typically using the USB cable they often find lying around in the cabin.
Most Kia Boys get inside these cars by breaking the side glass, but in some cases, they even find them unlocked. That’s specifically why police in many states have repeatedly told Kia and Hyundai owners to lock their cars when going inside.
Once they’re in the cabin, the Kia Boys rip off the steering wheel column to reach the ignition. Afterwards, it’s all a matter of seconds until they drive away.
Photo: Fox 2 Detroit on YouTUbe This is exactly the story behind this recent case in Ohio.
The owner of the Kia says she parked her car in front of a Kroger store and went inside. When she came out, the car was no longer there, and after searching for it twice throughout the entire parking lot, she figured out it was stolen.
The local media cites the woman as saying that she knew a Kia theft trend was happening, but she somehow ignored the repeated calls for patching. She also did not have insurance.
Kia and Hyundai released software updates to block the viral hack shortly after it made the news in 2022. The patch is free of charge and can be installed by any dealership. Customers whose cars can’t be patched are provided with a steering wheel lock.
Photo: Fox 2 Detroit on YouTUbe This Kia was stolen by two teenagers who drove away in seconds, eventually being spotted by a Ring camera not far from the Kroger store. While the camera couldn’t see their faces, the Kia is seen approaching a parked truck when the two teenagers decide to jump out directly from the moving vehicle.
The moving Kia eventually crashes into the truck, and the two teens run away on foot. The reason was that a police car was approaching, so they probably got scared, thinking the Kia was already reported as stolen. It wasn’t, and as it turns out, the police officers who were patrolling the neighborhood didn’t even see the Kia crashing into the truck.
The two teenagers escaped without anyone seeing them, so while the police are still investigating, there’s little chance they’ll even be identified.
Photo: WTHR on YouTube/Alissa Smart Police returned the Kia to the owner, who says that she’ll have to pay more than $700 to fix the damage caused by the teenagers. The vehicle exhibits the typical Kia Boys damage, with the ignition exposed and a cable inserted to start the engine.
The reason why Kias and Hyundais continue to be stolen using the 2022 TikTok trending method is that owners ignore all the calls to install the anti-theft update. The patch works, according to the two carmakers, and the only requirement is that owners lock their cars using the key fob. Once they do this, the engine no longer starts when the USB trick is being used.
Police in many other American regions also urged owners to patch their cars , also recommending that they install additional anti-theft protections, such as steering wheel locks.
These devices have so far proved to be the most effective against the Kia Boys, particularly because they could also prevent additional damage to the vehicle, such as shattered glass.
Photo: WTHR on YouTube/Alissa Smart Because these teenagers typically get inside a Kia by breaking a side window, a steering wheel lock could make them walk away before they break the glass. The club can be observed from outside the vehicle, so the Kia Boys could end up searching for a vehicle they can actually steal, rather than breaking a window for no reason.
Most of these teens steal cars for fun or joyrides, and because they have little to no driving experience, many stolen vehicles end up crashing into other parked cars, poles, or buildings. In some rare cases, the teenagers end up setting the vehicles on fire , recording the whole thing and posting it online for views.
Police also recommend that owners install anti-theft devices that could help recover the stolen cars before they are totalled. GPS trackers and AirTags could provide the officers with live location information, eventually making it easier to locate and catch the Kia Boys. The AirTags are pill-shaped devices that use nearby iPhones to broadcast their locations to the owner’s smartphone, and police say they can use this data to figure out where the thieves might be.

Alpina Prepping New 7er, Flagship Sedan Spied in a Premiere
24 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
The latest BMW 7 Series might trick some into thinking that it is entirely new, but it’s not. In fact, it is the mid-cycle refresh of the G70 that has been around since mid-2022, and it debuted some six months ago.
Fortunately, the Munich-based auto marque decided to keep it away from the Neue Klasse design language so far, which is why it looks evolutionary. And that’s definitely great news for those who do not fancy the Neue Klasse attire. And for what it’s worth, the next-generation X7 flagship SUV, which is expected to launch for the 2028 model year in the States, will also look like an evolution of the outgoing one.
Mind you, that is until you open the door, because both models feature the same interior. And as you likely know, the latest BMW 7 Series , or the LCI (Life Cycle Impulse) as the company calls it, benefits from the Panoramic iDrive. This is the pillar-to-pillar display at the bottom of the windshield. It’s joined by a 17.9-inch free-floating central display, a quirky-looking steering wheel, and a few other revisions that will probably not age that well.
To absolutely no one’s surprise, there will be no M7, as it is the new M760 xDrive that sits at the very top of the family. Unveiled earlier this month, it brings the V8 back to the brand’s flagship sedan. The automaker chose to keep the full specs close to its chest for now, but it did announce that the 4.4-liter twin-turbocharged mill produces around 570 horsepower. That’s a bit more than the old 760i, which had 563 horsepower available via the right pedal.
Photo: SH Proshots However, if you want an even punchier new BMW 7 Series and don’t fancy turning to the tuning world, then you will have to wait for Alpina to present its new take on the latest 7er. The model was recently spied testing in a premiere, and rumor has it that it is based on the M760 xDrive. This means that it will utilize the same engine, albeit with more output and torque.
The model will also be a lot faster than the standard one, and in plain Alpina fashion, it will benefit from a lot more goodies besides the upgraded powertrain that we do not know much about so far. Expect the usual chassis modifications, which will find the sweet spot between fast cornering and comfortable everyday driving, as well as probably uprated brakes to keep the extra oomph in check.
Spied in the open at the BMW M Test Center close to the Nurburgring in Germany, this new Alpina 7 was fully wrapped in camouflage. However, we can tell quite easily that it features an entirely new bumper at the front, as well as a new kidney grille. The side skirts are part of the Alpina makeover from what we can tell, and so is the rear bumper.
Other highlights will include the dedicated quad exhaust pipes, and the familiar Alpina wheels, with their multi-spoke design. Thus, we would not bet on the alloys equipping this prototype making their way to the production model. The famous blue and green colors will also be a thing, and we also expect some changes on the inside, likely comprising the Panoramic iDrive, the infotainment system, steering wheel, gear selector, and seats.
Photo: SH Proshots It is likely that Alpina will top off the upcoming 7er with dedicated upholstery and trim, and the model will also be decorated with the usual logos inside and out. Yellow daytime running lights also seem to be on deck, and between us, we cannot wait for the wraps to be removed in order to see this glorious sedan with its typical Alpina touches.
We do not yet know what it will be called, whether it will go by the Alpina 7 Series name, the Alpina 7, or the Alpina B7, just like its predecessor, but regardless of the name, it will be one extremely exciting sedan that will offer perfect balance between sporty and comfortable driving, not to mention great straight-line performance due to its extra oomph, exclusive colors on the outside, dedicated trim and upholstery in the cabin, and the famous Alpina wheels.
The model will boast its distinctive character, and will likely attract enthusiasts of all ages, including petrolheads who would not normally get a BMW 7 Series . And to no one’s surprise, it will sit at the very top of the latest 7er family in all markets, including the United States of America, where it might arrive for the 2028 model year. That’s what we believe anyway, and you shouldn’t quote us on that for obvious reasons.
Now, are you excited about the arrival of the all-new Alpina 7? Does this model look like your next go-to ride? What about a few years from now when you come across that perfectly-specified example on the used car market? Tell us all about it in the comments box below.

Google Maps "Fall Update" Now Rolling Out on Android Auto if You Are Really, Really Lucky
6 photos
Photo: Google
Google Maps is getting another update. That’s right, you’ve heard it correctly, but this time, it’s not something to be super-excited about for two reasons. First, it’s only a visual refresh, and second, it’s only aimed at only a small subset of users.
Google says it’s rolling out fall colors for Google Maps on Android Auto, therefore making the experience a little bit more realistic. However, this update doesn’t change all that much on your Android Auto screen, as the only facelift you’ll observe is the new color of the trees.
Google explains that the “trees in Google Maps will match the foliage while you’re driving,” and a video that previews this update provides us with a short look at this facelift.
Unfortunately, the video also reveals the reason why so many of us wouldn’t even get this fall update.
The fall colors on Google Maps are only available for users who received the immersive update. Announced earlier this year, the immersive navigation update completely transforms the experience with Google Maps, making the UI feel more realistic with see-through passes, trees, crosswalks, 3D views, and many other details that weren’t available earlier.
The immersive navigation update is similar in so many ways to the Apple Maps detailed city experience , which is still rolling out at an incredibly slow pace around the world. Google seemingly isn’t in a rush to bring this update to more users either, as not even everybody in the United States has received it.
The hardware configuration doesn’t make a difference, and it doesn’t increase your chances of getting immersive navigation. Users who bought a Google Pixel thinking they would be favored over others when new features roll out discovered that this isn’t the case the hard way, so even if they have a Google phone and live in the United States, they are still stuck with the previous Google Maps interface.
With immersive navigation enabled on such a small number of devices, the availability of this fall update is, therefore, very limited. There’s another reason why you might not even see the new colors, as Google says the facelift will appear only in “applicable US metros.”
As if all these limitations weren’t enough, the new colors will be there until November 30, so if you don’t see them in a few days, the chances are that they’ll never be there.
Meanwhile, immersive navigation is still rolling out, so fingers crossed that Google accelerates the release and brings it to more users, especially in non-US markets, as soon as possible. The search giant has never shared an ETA or a calendar for the release of immersive navigation, but it’s pretty obvious that the amount of work this update involves means broad availability cannot be reached overnight. now the trees in google maps will match the foliage while you’re driving available in applicable US metros until November 30. https://t.co/YHj2K3Ziun — Google Maps (@googlemaps) October 27, 2026

Looking for a biopharma job in New York? Jobs on BioSpace have soared year over year and month over month.
It may be getting easier for biopharma professionals to land positions in New York, based on BioSpace data. Job postings live on the BioSpace website for that section of the Pharm Country Hotbed soared 109% from Oct. 1, 2025, to Oct. 26, 2026. They also jumped month over month from August to September (+32%) and September to October (+19% through Oct. 26).
If you’re interested in working at a biopharma in New York, check out the open roles at these eight companies.
Regeneron has around 300 positions available. Jobs include senior principal scientist, bispecifics and antibody engineering in Tarrytown; senior device development engineer-product design in East Greenbush; and quality control analyst in Rensselaer.
Amgen has about 20 openings. Roles include senior medical science liaison, inflammation-CT/NY in Manhattan; senior oncology specialist-Sapphire Lower Manhattan in New York City; and regional patient access lead-North East in New York City.
Syngene has several positions available in Baltimore. Jobs include senior process engineer; manager-facilities; and director-engineering and maintenance.
Sanofi has multiple openings in Pearl River. Roles include manager, GMP facility, asset readiness and HSE; deputy director manufacturing operations; and production technician.
Daiichi Sankyo is hiring an oncology territory manager, breast-Albany in Albany and an oncology territory manager, breast-Long Island/Queens/Brooklyn in New York City.
Lundbeck has openings for a multispecialty account manager-Rochester, NY, in Rochester and a psychiatry account manager-Schenectady-NY in Schenectady.
AbbVie is hiring an MSL field medical director, oncology-Northeast in New York City.

Cadillac CTS-V Races Twin-Turbo C8 Corvette, Loser Should've Stayed Put – Video
6 photos
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Import 2 Race
Unlike other American automakers, Cadillac remains committed to traditional passenger cars, as it has quite a few sedans in its current lineup in the States.
These include the CT4 and the CT5, as well as their sport-oriented V-Series derivatives, as well as the Celestiq. Other than that, it is pretty much a crossover/SUV fest, some of which feature electric firepower. And it’s more of the latter when it comes to Chevrolet, which offers plenty high-riders, as well as some trucks, and zero traditional passenger cars.
However, the bowtie brand , which operates under the roof of General Motors, just like Cadillac, in case you forgot, does have a huge ace up its sleeve when it comes to performance-oriented models. It’s called the Corvette, and it comprises quite a few models. The latest version of the Stingray packs an LS6 6.7-liter small-block V8 that pushes out 535 hp (543 ps/399 kW) and 520 lb-ft (705 Nm) of torque.
It takes just 2.8 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill, deals with the quarter mile in 11 seconds at 124 mph (200 kph), and despite its blue-blooded performance, it starts from a very decent $71,300 for the 2027 model year. The Grand Sport shares the same engine, kicking off at $86,300, and the Grand Sport X, which replaced the E-Ray, has 721 hp (731 ps/538 kW), drops the sprint time to a mere 2.4 seconds, and starts at $110,000.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Import 2 Race The Z06 remains the same track-focused tool that everyone knows, boasting 670 horsepower (679 ps/499 kW), and taking 2.6 seconds to reach 60 mph. It has an MSRP of $121,800 for the 2027 model year. The crazy ZR1 and ZR1X have 1,064 hp (1,079 ps/794 kW) and 1,250 hp (1,267 ps/932 kW), respectively, taking 2.3 seconds to hit 60 mph for the former and 1.89 seconds for the latter, and can be ordered from $198,000 and $227,800, respectively.
This story is partially about the C8-generation Chevrolet Corvette Z06, not in general, as the example shared on video at the bottom of the page recently stepped under the spotlight. As we already told you, this model has 670 hp (680 ps/500 kW) from its flat-plane crank 5.5-liter V8, and 460 pound-feet (624 Nm) of torque. It zips to 60 mph in just 2.6 seconds, and the standing quarter mile is a 10.6-second affair, with an exit speed of 131 mph (211 kph), the spec sheet reveals.
However, this particular car has been visited by the tuning fairy, as it boasts a twin-turbocharged conversion, albeit with undisclosed output, torque, and performance. This is what the description of the video embedded at the end of this story says, anyway. And this Z06 faced a Cadillac CTS-V for a straight-line duel, as mentioned in the title.
The four-door sedan is part of the second generation, and as you likely recall, this model shared its lump with the C6 Chevy Corvette ZR1. Therefore, we are talking about a V8 with supercharging and a 6.2-liter displacement, which was officially rated at 556 hp (564 ps/415 kW) and 551 lb-ft (747 Nm) of torque back when the car was new.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Import 2 Race Mind you, although it is fast, the Cadillac CTS-V won’t blow your socks off compared to today’s sporty vehicles, as the 0 to 60 mph sprint takes around four seconds. That’s definitely unimpressive by today’s standards, but keep in mind that this model was developed more than two decades ago. Production spanned between 2007 and 2014, and besides the four-door sedan, Caddy also offered it as a five-door station wagon, and a two-door coupe.
A quick comparison between the second-generation Cadillac CTS-V and the C8 Chevrolet Corvette Z06 reveals that the balance tilts in favor of the latter, and that’s before any outside intervention from the tuning world. However, as we already told you in the above paragraphs, the Corvette in question has indeed been visited by the tuning fairy, and according to the video uploader, it has a twin-turbocharged conversion, which is why it goes like stink.
Mind you, the its four-door rival on that day did not make a fool of itself either, and that means that it has probably been modified as well, because it can definitely keep up with the crazy Chevy. But is it punchy and fast enough in order to put the Corvette in its corner? That is for you to find out by scrolling down and clicking the play button on the video shared by Import 2 Race.
The footage is less than half a minute long, so you will find out which of these machines came out victorious on that day. By the way, it’s a drag race from a 45 mph (72 kph) rolling start, in case you were wondering, so that these two can better put down the power. That said, enjoy!

2026 SEMA Show • 2027 Dodge Charger Gets Special-Edition Package Celebrating 90 Years of Mopar
1964 Chrysler 300 Parked for Decades Emerges As Family-Owned Survivor
15 photos
Photo: Facebook Marketplace/Rita Rinderle
In 1955, Chrysler introduced the C-300 , a flagship high-performance coupe. The car spawned what we now know as the 300 letter series; it remained in production through 1965. But it wasn't the only Mopar to sport the "300" badge during its time in showrooms. In 1962, Chrysler debuted a second 300 model.
It was more affordable than the letter series and lacked some of the exclusive features that made the latter stand out. Moreover, it wasn't restricted to two-door body styles. Chrysler also offered a four-door hardtop and added a sedan to the lineup in 1965. The 300 also lacked the exclusive high-performance powerplant of the letter series.
The non-letter series remained in production until 1971, and, needless to say, it sold in greater numbers due to its more affordable sticker. Specifically, Chrysler sold over 270,000 units over 10 model years. For reference, the 300 letter series moved only 16,981 examples over 11 model years.
But a higher production number also means limited desirability. And unlike the letter series, the regular 300 is more common in junkyards nowadays. Most of them have morphed into rust buckets, but some were lucky enough to soldier on for decades without notable damage. This 1964 two-door hardtop is one of those cars.
The Mopar surfaced in Versailles, Ohio, after an extended period of time in a barn. It's unclear when it was parked, but it may have been decades based on the reading on the odometer. The latter shows only 42,800 miles (68,880 km). But while it may have been sitting for 30 or 40 years, the Chrysler is still in very good condition.
Sure, there's some surface rust, the paint has seen better days, and the interior is dusty, but I've seen vehicles with more damage after a notably shorter time off the road. Fortunately, this car was parked off the ground, which helped keep the frame safe from rust and the interior free of rodents.
Another cool thing about this Chrysler is that it's been in the same family since it was new. This probably explains why it received proper maintenance over the years. The numbers-matching 383-cubic-inch (6.3-liter) V8 engine is still under the hood, but there's no word on whether it runs.
The standard mill in the 300 non-letter series at the time, the two-barrel 383 V8 came with a solid 305 horsepower on tap. Chrysler also offered an optional 413-cubic-inch (6.8-liter) V8 good for 360 horsepower.
How rare is this Mopar? Well, Chrysler sold quite a few of them in 1964: exactly 26,887 rolled off the assembly line. About half of these vehicles were two-door hardtops. Specifically, this 300 is one of 13,401 produced (possibly under 10,000 with the 383-cubic-inch V8).
The barn find is available for $5,000 , which isn't much for a classic of this caliber. On the flip side, it will cost a pretty penny to get the V8 running again and refresh the car inside and out.

W206 Mercedes-Benz C-Class Arrives in the United States During H1 of 2027 With a Single Powertrain
12 photos
Photo: Mercedes-Benz
Independent of the W520 Mercedes-Benz C-Class Electric , the combustion-powered W206 fifth generation has been refreshed earlier this year to stand alongside the bigger GLE and GLS or the S-Class; now it’s announced to arrive in the United States during the first half of next year in a single powertrain version.
The Mercedes-Benz C-Class (W206), the fifth generation of the executive compact car originally arrived in 2021 and during the summer of 2026 it received a comprehensive update to bring it in line with some of the latest facelifts like the S-Class and the GLE plus GLE Coupe twins, as well as the GLS, adopting the new illuminated grille, the three-pointed star design of the front and rear lamps, plus a revised interior.
The company says the latest Mercedes‑Benz C‑Class “introduces the most comprehensive update to date for its best-selling sedan model family” with a sporty style, an elegant cockpit, intuitive technology and an agile, efficient powertrain. It has a sharper visual presence, additional creature comforts, expanded technology, and a high-tech electrified combustion engine, at least for the US automotive market.
“The new C‑Class proves that continuity and innovation are not mutually exclusive. With its sporty elegance, electrified high-tech powertrain and intelligent support powered by MB.OS, it delivers what drivers truly need: proven reliability and innovative technology that creates real added value in everyday life. In this way, a familiar classic becomes a modern companion,” explains Mathias Geisen, Member of the Board of Management of Mercedes-Benz Group AG.
The popular Mercedes was introduced in 1982 and has been a defining model for the compact executive segment, with more than twelve million vehicles sold globally – in America, the latest C-Class is coming to US dealerships during the first half of 2027 with the 2027 Mercedes-Benz C 350 and C 350 4Matic options – a single powertrain but with either RWD or all-wheel drive.
The sedan has a new radiator grille with contour lighting and an illuminated central Mercedes-Benz star, headlamps with the star element, two new colors, three new trim options, an optional Burmester 3D Surround Sound System that has been enhanced, an electrified combustion engine, a more refined suspension, and the new Mercedes-Benz Operating System (MB.OS) running the tasks inside the cockpit with over-the-air updates for the entire vehicle software suite.
The newest MBUX also introduces the AI-based MBUX Virtual Assistant, an “intelligent assistant (that) can engage in complex conversations and has short-term memory, responding like a well-informed friend.” Intelligent navigation is now based on Google technology, together with MBUX Surround Navigation, and there’s also a new multifunction steering wheel with more ergonomic controls along with standard MB.DRIVE, PARKING ASSIST 360, and other advanced driver and parking assistance systems.
The sole powertrain option is the updated 2.0-liter M 254 EVO four-cylinder engine featuring a 48-volt electrical system, packing 255 hp and 295 lb-ft of torque. There’s an overboost function that comes with an additional 27 hp for approximately 20 seconds. Also, the second-generation integrated starter-generator (ISG 2.0) helps the engine at low speeds with up to 23 hp and 151 lb-ft.
The 48-volt electrical system has integrated functions such as coasting and recuperation to help maximize efficiency: “ISG 2.0 enables the transition from coasting with the engine switched off to powerful propulsion under engine power as well as operation of the start-stop function to be almost imperceptible to the driver.”

source_document.body:
As companies invest billions of dollars to reshore manufacturing, 10 biotech and pharma businesses are reportedly trimming staff at manufacturing locations in 2026 or the coming years, with BioNTech having the deepest cuts.
This year’s made or planned layoffs at biotech and pharma manufacturing facilities stand to put at least 4,000 people out of work, based on BioSpace tallies. Through Oct. 28, 10 biopharmas cut or projected they would cut 4,062 employees at their plants, several of which are shuttering.
The BioNTech workforce is taking the biggest hit, as the Germany-based biotech’s expected layoffs will affect 1,860 people . In a quarterly report released in May, the company disclosed it plans to exit multiple manufacturing sites because they will become underused or idle in the next 24 months. BioNTech expects to shutter facilities in Idar-Oberstein and Marburg, Germany, by the end of 2027, affecting about 440 and 540 positions, respectively, and in Singapore in Q1 2027, impacting around 60 jobs.
BioNTech also plans to exit CureVac’s German and international sites by the end of 2027, affecting about 820 roles. BioNTech acquired CureVac last year in a $1.25 billion all-stock deal.
Layoffs
BioNTech moves to close multiple manufacturing plants, affecting 1,860 jobs
The action affects BioNTech sites in Germany and Singapore, where the company expects to have excess capacity.

Biopharma companies’ made and planned manufacturing facility layoffs did not surprise Eric Langer, managing partner and president of BioPlan Associates, which provides biopharma and healthcare market information and research services. In an emailed response to BioSpace , Langer put the numbers into perspective.
“Surgical cuts are not uncommon occurrences, and an average of 300 staff per company at large organizations may not have a major impact on overall biopharma operations,” he said.
Caitlin Prendes, vice president of CMC at Abcentra, a Los Angeles–based biotech, told BioSpace in an emailed response that the layoff numbers are concerning but not surprising given the pressures and environment biotechs and pharmas face. Companies, she said, are responding to changes in product demand, preparing for upcoming major patent cliffs and reacting to clinical and regulatory setbacks, including recent trial failures. At the same time, Prendes noted, they’re trying to find ways to fund new assets while cutting costs.
“Policy uncertainty adds complexity to those decisions, while AI and automation offer opportunities to improve productivity—although I wouldn’t assume they are driving the layoffs we are seeing today,” she added.
Regarding what is driving biopharmas’ manufacturing facility layoffs this year, Prendes said the most direct drivers could be changes in specific product demand, product setbacks and company-specific restructuring.
“Manufacturing capacity is built around expectations for particular medicines,” she said. “Those expectations can change due to low commercial demand, clinical trial failures, or a myriad of other reasons. When capacity exceeds demand, companies may have more capacity than they can sustainably support, leading to layoffs and site closures.”
Prendes added that patent cliffs add pressure because companies must prepare for potential reduction in revenue and demand while simultaneously investing in replacement products. That, she said, can lead to outcomes including consolidation and outsourcing to contract development and manufacturing organizations.
Several layoffs take place alongside reshoring efforts
Of the 10 biopharmas making or planning cuts, five have made manufacturing investments of $1 billion or more in the past three years: Gilead, GSK, Merck and Pfizer in 2025 and Novo in 2024. All but Novo made their commitments after President Donald Trump’s 2025 threat to levy tariffs on companies that don’t reshore manufacturing operations.
Merck and Pfizer have committed to the largest investments. Pfizer made its announcement first, at the end of September 2025. The New York–based pharma committed $70 billion to U.S. research, development and capital projects. While Pfizer did not specifically say the money would go toward manufacturing, Trump described the commitment as an investment in reshoring domestic manufacturing facilities .
New Jersey–based Merck made its announcement in October 2025. The pharma committed to investing more than $70 billion to expand U.S. manufacturing and research and development. That investment included construction of a $3 billion, 400,000-square-foot pharmaceutical manufacturing facility at Merck’s Elkton, Virginia, site. The move was expected to potentially add more than 500 full-times roles at the facility.
However, as Prendes noted, a shift to more domestic production doesn’t ensure that a given U.S. facility will continue to grow. Pfizer’s projected cuts at manufacturing sites include letting go of around 150 employees in Portage, Michigan, MLive reported. The pharma’s statement to MLive connected those cuts to lower projected demand for some products manufactured at the facility.
In addition, Pfizer will lay off an undisclosed number of staff at the pharma’s Rocky Mount and Sanford, North Carolina, manufacturing sites, according to the Triangle Business Journal .
Merck, meanwhile, laid off 147 employees at its vaccine manufacturing plant in Durham, North Carolina, effective May 1. The cuts were disclosed in a February Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act notice .
Neither Langer nor Prendes found it unusual that companies are working to reshore manufacturing operations while also trimming staff.
“Companies may reduce capacity for an older asset approaching loss of exclusivity while investing in a separate facility for a new product or modality with different manufacturing requirements,” Prendes explained. She also noted that there is a timing issue, as layoffs at existing sites can happen years before new facilities begin staffing up.
“Domestic investment and workforce reductions can be simultaneous,” she said.
Manufacturing facility layoffs could continue in 2027
More layoffs at biopharma companies’ manufacturing facilities could be ahead in 2027, according to Langer. He noted that BioPlan Associates’ 2026 report on biopharma manufacturing capacity and production showed that the number of bioprocessing professionals saying that manufacturing productivity/efficiency improvements are needed rose from 14.6% in 2025 to 20.9% this year. That, he said, indicates a ramped-up focus on costs and productivity.
“I would expect this trend to continue into 2027,” Langer said. “If an operation can be automated, or more can be produced with fewer staff, then facilities have clearly indicated they will move in that direction.”
Layoff numbers exclude contract development and manufacturing organizations, contract research organizations, tools and services businesses and medical device firms. To tally the cuts, BioSpace compiles data for known workforce reductions. The number of employees affected is identified or estimated through confirmation from company officials as well as information in company press releases, Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act notices, SEC filings and media outlets’ reports.
Not all companies disclose downsizing, and some share only the percentage of staff affected. Some biopharmas provide total numbers retrospectively rather than disclosing individual workforce reductions as they happen.
